head_commit.message:
[fix] Use canonical timezone names in Python unit tests (#17567)

Fixes Python unit tests on CI, which fail since `ubuntu-latest` moved to
the Ubuntu 26.04 image: `column_config_utils_test.py` errors during
collection with `ZoneInfoNotFoundError: 'No time zone found with key
US/Central'`, which aborts the whole pytest run.

- Ubuntu 26.04's `tzdata` package no longer ships legacy aliases such as
`US/Central` and `US/Pacific` (they moved to the separate
`tzdata-legacy` package), and pandas 3 only installs the `tzdata` Python
package on Windows, so Linux runners have no source for these keys.
- Replaces `US/Central` with its canonical name `America/Chicago`, and
drops the `US/Pacific` case in `hashing_test.py` because it is an alias
of `America/Los_Angeles`, which the next case already covers.
- Doesn't add `tzdata` to the dev dependencies: that would make CI pass
while hiding tests that depend on deprecated aliases.
- Includes a bot snapshot refresh (#17568) of 36 chromium `st_map` /
`st_pydeck_chart` snapshots. These map tests also fail on `develop` (run
39389190040) since the runner image change, independent of the timezone
fix.

N/A. Failing `develop` run:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/actions/runs/39379917716

- Test-only change; no additional tests needed.
- Ran the full Python unit suite locally with `PYTHONTZPATH` pointing at
a zoneinfo directory that matches the Ubuntu 26.04 `tzdata` package
(continent and `Etc/` zones plus `UTC`, `GMT`, `Factory`). Before the
fix it reproduces the CI collection error plus a `US/Pacific` failure in
`hashing_test.py`; after the fix there are no timezone errors.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**

>
> **Overview**
> Updates Python unit tests so they use **IANA canonical timezone
names** instead of legacy `US/*` aliases that Ubuntu 26.04 CI no longer
provides in default `tzdata`.
>
> In `column_config_utils_test.py`, timezone-aware datetime fixtures
switch from `US/Central` to **`America/Chicago`**, avoiding
`ZoneInfoNotFoundError` during pytest collection on `ubuntu-latest`.
>
> In `hashing_test.py`, the parameterized `test_pandas_timestamp` cases
drop **`US/Pacific`** because it duplicates coverage already provided by
`America/Los_Angeles`. No production/runtime code changes—test-only
alignment with modern zoneinfo data.
